title: Touch on-foot analog: analog move/turn through shared CharacterInput + physics
description: On foot, the wire thrust/yaw are already analog floats but inputToCharacterInput thresholds them at ±0.5 into booleans, so 15-50% of the stick is dead and 50-100% is full walk speed — the same binary feel as the flight sticks, one layer deeper. This task makes CharacterInput analog (move −1..1 forward-positive, turn −1..1 left-positive matching the existing left/right semantics, run/jump stay booleans), scales walk speed and turn rate by magnitude in the shared integrateCharacter, passes the wire values through (clamped for cheat-resistance), merges the touch MOVE stick magnitudes with the keyboard in the client on-foot loop (reusing TASK-99's mergeAxis), and keeps the keyboard path byte-for-byte at full magnitude (keyboard sends ±1 ⇒ identical states to today). PRD §4.14 / M7 goal: linear on-foot touch movement, SC-6.
steps: Read app/src/shared/physics/character.ts (CharacterInput, integrateCharacter, characterSubstep — note the TASK-80 turn sign convention: left = +rotation about Y), app/src/shared/protocol/inputs.ts (inputToCharacterInput 0.5 thresholds + TASK-55 sensitivity comment), the on-foot loop in app/src/client/main.tsx (~lines 1697-1736), app/src/client/net/character-prediction.ts (ZERO_CHARACTER_INPUT), and grep for every Consumer of CharacterInput.forward/back/left/right.

In app/src/shared/physics/character.ts: replace forward/back/left/right booleans with `move: number` (forward-positive, −1..1) and `turn: number` (screen-left-positive, −1..1); keep run/jump booleans. In characterSubstep: turning = rotate by +CHAR_TURN_RATE*turn*h when turn>0, −CHAR_TURN_RATE*|turn|*h when turn<0 (0 = no turn); movement: when move ≠ 0 set horizontal velocity along the facing * sign(move) at speed (run ? CHAR_RUN_SPEED : CHAR_WALK_SPEED) * |move|; move = 0 keeps the friction path. Update ZERO_CHARACTER_INPUT and every field reference (server shard only uses inputToCharacterInput, so it follows automatically).

In app/src/shared/protocol/inputs.ts: inputToCharacterInput passes the wire thrust → move and yaw → turn CLAMPED to [−1, 1] (cheat-resistance — a spoofed move=100 must not yield 100× speed; consistent with TASK-67), replacing the 0.5 thresholds. Update the doc comment: the client pre-scales yaw by the TASK-55 sensitivity (0.5x..2x), so at 0.5x a full keyboard press turns at half rate (new, intended) and at 1x/2x the clamped value is 1.0 (keyboard 1x unchanged).

In the on-foot loop in app/src/client/main.tsx: build the keyboard thrust/yaw booleans as today, merge each with touchRef.current.snapshot() via mergeAxis (from app/src/client/input/touch.ts, TASK-99) so a partial MOVE stick rides the wire, keep the sensitivity multiplication on the merged yaw, run/jump unchanged. The payload shape is unchanged (InputPayload is already analog).

Update app/src/client/net/character-prediction.ts ZERO_CHARACTER_INPUT to the new shape and any tests/fixtures that build CharacterInput literals (grep). The existing character golden tests fed full-magnitude input (±1 / true) must pass with UNCHANGED expected states — that is the keyboard-parity proof.

Unit tests: integrateCharacter with move=0.5 → horizontal speed 0.5× full walk (±2% tolerance, flat terrain, no run); move=−0.5 → 0.5× backward; turn=±0.5 → half the facing delta of turn=±1 over the same dt; move=0 + friction unchanged. inputToCharacterInput: thrust=0.5 → move=0.5, yaw=2 → turn clamped to 1, thrust=100 → move clamped to 1. Keyboard parity: move=1/turn=1/run/jump true produces the exact states the old boolean input produced (keep at least one legacy golden assertion).

E2E (extend app/tests/e2e/touch-onfoot.spec.ts, same __TOUCH__.move pattern): server-reported character horizontal speed at __TOUCH__.move({thrust: 0.5}) is within [0.4, 0.6]× the full-thrust speed and > 0; __TOUCH__.move({thrust: 1}) equals the full speed (regression); partial turn ({yaw: 0.5}) rotates the server-reported facing at ~half rate of {yaw: 1} (band [0.4, 0.6]× over a fixed time).

Run the full gate: npm test, npm run typecheck, eslint + prettier on touched files, npx playwright test tests/e2e/touch-onfoot.spec.ts + tests/e2e/touch-loop.spec.ts, then commit (Conventional Commit).
acceptanceCriteria: Unit tests prove: partial move/turn magnitudes scale character speed and turn rate proportionally; wire mapping clamps to [−1, 1]; full-magnitude (±1 / true) inputs produce byte-identical states to the pre-task boolean input (keyboard parity, golden tests unchanged).
touch-onfoot.spec.ts e2e: server-reported speed at partial stick (0.5) is strictly between rest and full speed and within [0.4, 0.6]× full; partial turn rotates at ~half rate.
npm test + typecheck + lint green; touch-loop.spec.ts (SC-1 loop) and the flight touch specs still green; one commit.
notes: Depends on TASK-99 (mergeAxis lives in app/src/client/input/touch.ts). The server shard needs no code change beyond what flows through inputToCharacterInput — verify by grep, not assumption. Character prediction and server both call the shared integrateCharacter, so keeping them in lock step is automatic once the shared module is analog. Do not change CHAR_* constants, jump physics, or the friction path. The 0.5-wire-threshold comment in inputs.ts must be rewritten, not left stale.
